conviction_note: Seven small, mostly macro and peer-proxy findings that roughly cancel. Higher rates help NII and the forward guide (asset sensitivity about 10%, PNC raised its outlook on the same rate path) but hurt AOCI, tangible book and how fast buybacks come back. The Q3 lines sit inside a guide reaffirmed on 2026-09-15, and the last beat-and-raise was sold (-2.29%). So p_up is 52 and abs_move is 3.5: above the name's 1.31% median because sector volatility is high, below the 6.12% option-implied move, which looks inflated by sector IV (ATM 30.6 against 16.1 realised). That gives +0.14 against an impact_sum of +0.10. The two measurements agree, both are near zero, and neither is decisive.

findings.finding: Rates are now above what FITB's guide assumed. The July guide assumed one 25bp hike in September off the end-of-June forward curve. That hike came on 2026-09-16 (to 3.75-4.00%), and PNC's 2026-10-15 baseline now assumes two more (December 2026 and March 2027, to 4.25-4.50%). FITB disclosed year-two asset sensitivity of just under 10% plus fixed-rate asset repricing. PNC, on the same rate path, raised its FY26 NII outlook to about +15.5% (from 15-15.5%) and guided 4Q26 NII up about 4%. So a raised or firmed 4Q26/2027 NII outlook from FITB on 10-19 is more likely than the FY guide of $8.74-8.80bn implies.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last print (2026-07-17) FITB raised its FY NII guide to $8.74-8.80bn, cut expense guidance and beat EPS ($1.02 against $0.98), and the stock fell 2.29%, so this name has recently sold a raise. Of the last seven prints, four were up, with a median absolute move of 1.31%.
findings.why_not_priced: The hike and the curve are public. What is not public is FITB's own translation: the July guide was built on a curve with one hike, and FITB has not updated its full-year number since (on 09-15 it said 'unchanged from July 17'). If the market had priced a raise, FITB would have outperformed KRE since PNC's 10-15 raise. FITB closed 10-15 at +1.4% against KRE +1.8%, and has lagged KRE by about 4.6 points since July.
findings.independence: FITB's own sensitivity disclosure is in the Q2 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/17/fifth-third-fitb-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/): asset sensitivity just under 10%, and the guide assumed a September hike. The rate path is in the PNC deck. A Zacks snippet (date not verified, snippet_only) has the CFO at Barclays calling FITB 'fairly well positioned' for higher rates: https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2994708/. This is a proxy: FITB itself has not confirmed a raise.

findings.finding: Q3 AOCI and tangible book will take a hit from the long end. The 10-year went from about 4.4% in late June (4.41% on 06-24) to about 5.1-5.2% by late September and 5.24% on 10-09. FITB entered the quarter with AOCI of -$3.345bn, CET1 including AOCI of 8.7%, TCE including AOCI of 7.3%, TBV of $23.15, and $44.5bn of AFS securities. Peers who reported this week showed the size of it: PNC's AOCI went from -$4.1bn to -$6.5bn and TBV fell 3.1%, and Regions' TBV fell 8.2% ($13.78 to $12.65). A visible TBV decline and a lower AOCI-inclusive capital ratio raise the risk that the H2 buyback restart (guided as a smaller Q3, then $200-300m a quarter in Q4) is deferred or trimmed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nothing in the baseline isolates this line. In Q2 2026 the CET1 rise to 9.93% with no buybacks in H1 did not stop a -2.29% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Rates are public and the KBW bank index fell 9.7% in the month to 10-12, so the sector-wide AOCI hit is largely in the price. What is not known is FITB's own number, its hedge offset, and whether management sticks with the Q4 $200-300m buyback pace. If that were priced, FITB would trade at a discount to its own TBV path. Instead it has tracked KRE since mid-September.
findings.independence: PNC Q3 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000713676/000162828026065936/q32026financialhighlightsa.htm): AOCI -$6.5bn against -$4.1bn, TBV -3.1%, CET1 9.8% from 9.9%, while PNC kept its buybacks at $0.6bn and guided Q4 at the same level, which cuts against the deferral half of this finding and is why it is sized small. FITB's starting AOCI figures are from the Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000035527/000003552726000193/q22026earningsrelease.htm). Rates: https://capital.com/en-eu/news/five-big-banks-two-days-one-question-can-record-trading. This is macro-to-company transmission.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-15, one week after the Comerica conversion, FITB reaffirmed every 3Q26 guide line as 'unchanged from July 17': NII up 2-2.5% from $2.22bn, average loans up about 1%, fees up 1-3%, expenses down 1-2%, NCOs 30-35bp. A Zacks snippet of the same appearance has the CFO saying deposit growth was stronger than expected. Peers that have printed landed NII inside comparable ranges (PNC +2.4% q/q, Regions +1.6%). The reported quarter is therefore likely in line with a bar the company set itself.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FITB beat EPS in Q2 2026 ($1.02 against $0.98) and fell 2.29%. Reactions on in-line or beat quarters have been small, with a median absolute move of 1.31% over seven prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: consensus revenue of $3.33-3.34bn is the guide's midpoint. The part the market may not have weighed is that the guide held through quarter-end after the conversion; the deposit-growth remark is snippet-only. This finding sits inside the guide, so it is sized near 0.
findings.independence: The deposit remark is snippet-only from https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2994708/ (could not be fetched, date not verified). Peer NII: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001281761/000128176126000063/rf-2026930xexhibit991.htm. Shares the 09-15 deck with no other finding.

Truist was +2.2% on 10-15 and +1.1% intraday on its 10-16 print, despite a $1.45bn securities loss. Regions was +0.5% intraday on its 10-16 print. PNC was -0.4% on its 10-15 print despite a raised outlook. The money-centres fell on 10-13: WFC -1.3% after an NII miss, JPM, C and GS all red. FITB enters having lagged KRE by about 4.6 points since its Q2 print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline line for this. In Q2 2026, peers' beat-and-raise prints were sold and FITB was sold too (-2.29%), so peer tone has carried over to FITB before.
findings.why_not_priced: Peer tone is visible to everyone, and FITB rose 1.4% with the group on 10-15, so this is partly priced. What is left is the relative underperformance since July: if the market had closed it, FITB would have outperformed KRE this week, and it has not.

findings.finding: Peers show commercial deposit pressure under rising rates. Regions' average deposits fell 1.2% q/q ($1.55bn), mainly as large corporate clients moved balances off balance sheet, and PNC's interest-bearing deposit rate rose 7bp to 1.98%. FITB's acquired Comerica franchise is heavily commercial and noninterest-bearing. On the Q2 call FITB said deposit costs would be 'stable to slightly up' and 'it certainly is getting more expensive to grow deposits'. That is a risk to Q4 NIM and to the deposit-mix commentary on 10-19.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 analysts pushed on deposit competition and beta (BofA, UBS, Goldman) and the stock fell 2.29% on the day, though the cause was not established.
findings.why_not_priced: Regions' outflow was published only this morning (10-16), and FITB's commercial-deposit exposure through Comerica is larger than most peers'. If it were priced, FITB would have traded down on Regions' print today, but it is up modestly intraday with the group.
findings.independence: PNC deposit rate in the deck (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000713676/000162828026065997/a3q26earningsslides_vfx2.htm). Cutting the other way: PNC spot deposits rose 4%, and the snippet-only Zacks report has FITB's CFO calling deposit growth stronger than expected (see finding 3). That offset is why this is sized small. Proxy.

findings.finding: The Comerica systems conversion (about 600k accounts and 293 branches, completed 2026-09-08) produced visible customer friction in Detroit and Dallas: account-access problems, crowded lobbies, long phone waits, the legacy app retired, bill-pay complaints, and a fraud warning. There is no evidence of deposit attrition or of a lasting outage after the first days.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior conversion print in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: These were local TV reports, not wire stories. If attrition had been material, FITB would have reported deposit softness at the 09-15 conference instead of reaffirming its guide. The finding is mostly a question for the call.
findings.independence: https://www.wxyz.com/news/fifth-third-banks-merger-with-comerica-frustrates-local-customers and https://www.nbcdfw.com/news/local/comerica-customer-accounts-close-and-transition-to-fifth-third/4072803/. Cutting against it: the 09-15 deck reaffirmed the guide and the synergy target (finding 3).

findings.finding: Peer credit in Q3 2026 was benign to mixed, with no new NDFI or fraud event found in 2026. Regions' NCOs fell to 0.29% from 0.42%, its business criticized ratio fell to 4.71% from 5.01%, and its NPLs fell to 0.59%. PNC's NCOs were 0.28% (from 0.25%) with commercial NPLs up 8%. FITB guides 2H NCOs at 30-35bp, and its NDFI book is about 7% of loans, with private credit and BDCs under 1%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The October 2025 print (+1.31%) carried the roughly $178m Tricolor fraud loss and was still bought. FITB has absorbed a credit one-off before.
findings.why_not_priced: Small. Credit fear was the 2025 sector driver. If this quarter's benign peer credit were fully priced, the bank index would not have fallen 9.7% in a month, though most of that fall is rates. The NDFI tail is the downside (a single-name fraud is not visible in advance), which is why the range is skewed negative.
findings.independence: PNC credit metrics: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000713676/000162828026065997/a3q26earningsslides_vfx2.htm. FITB's NDFI share is from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/17/fifth-third-fitb-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). Proxy.

baseline_tension: The evidence agrees with a balanced skew (-1.13, call side slightly bid) and a modest negative run-up: rate tailwinds to NII and rate headwinds to AOCI roughly offset. The 6.12% implied move looks more like sector IV than an FITB-specific risk, so abs_move is set at 3.5, not 6.1.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (reaction veto): FITB sold its Q2 beat-and-raise (-2.29%), so the rate/NII-guide finding went from +0.6 to +0.4 and p_up from 53 to 52.

Rule 5 (macro transmission is a small finding): the AOCI/tangible-book finding was trimmed from -0.5 to -0.4, because PNC held its buyback pace despite the same AOCI hit, which cuts against the deferral half.
Rule 6 (a finding inside the guide goes toward 0): the reaffirmed Q3 guide went from +0.2 to +0.1. The bar is sourced to the company guide plus two agreeing adjusted estimates, so no cap.
Rule 7 (positioning): short interest is low and falling (3.4-4.7% of float) and the skew is balanced, so no negative was shrunk for squeeze risk.
Left standing: peer tone (+0.3), deposit pressure (-0.3), conversion friction (-0.1), peer credit (+0.1).
